t.7.79.1: Having heard that tale concerning Ila, narrated by Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata were both supremely astonished.
t.7.79.2: Then the two, with joined palms in reverence, once more asked Rāma for a full account of the condition of that great-souled king.
t.7.79.3: How did that king, having become a woman, endure his wretched plight? And when he had become a man again, what manner of life did he lead?
t.7.79.4: Having heard those words of the two, filled with curiosity, Kākutstha recounted to them the story of that king just as it had happened.
t.7.79.6: Swiftly entering that forest, thick with trees, shrubs and creepers, the lotus-petal-eyed lady, the beauty of the world, roamed about on foot.
t.7.79.5: For that very first month, having become a woman, the fairest in all the world, she was surrounded by those women who had formerly been his followers, walking in his footsteps.
t.7.79.7: Then, having left behind all her mounts on every side, Ilā took her pleasure there in that wide hollow of the mountain.
t.7.79.8: Then, in that region of the forest, not far from the mountain, there was a lake of most lovely appearance, thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds.
t.7.79.9: Then Ilā saw there Budha, the son of Soma, blazing with his own form like the full moon that has risen.
t.7.79.10: They saw him performing fierce austerity in the midst of the waters, hard to approach, a bringer of renown, able to go wherever he wished, and established in the fullness of youth.
t.7.79.11: Astonished, she stirred up that whole lake together with those who had formerly been men and had now become women, O Raghunandana.
t.7.79.12: But Budha, the moment he beheld her, was sorely smitten by the arrows of Kāma; he could not then master himself, and he trembled there in the water.
t.7.79.13: Gazing at the lovely Ilā, whose beauty surpassed all the three worlds, he fell deep into thought: “Who can this be, a woman excelling even the goddesses?”
t.7.79.14: Neither among goddesses, nor among Nāga women, nor among Asura women and Apsarases have I ever before seen any woman adorned with such beauty as this.
t.7.79.15: "She would be a fitting match for me, if she does not belong to another." Having resolved thus, he came out of the water onto the land.
t.7.79.17: That righteous-souled one asked them: "Whose is this beauty of the world, and for what purpose has she come here? Tell me the truth without delay."
t.7.79.16: Having reached his hermitage, the righteous-souled one then called four of the young women, and they paid homage to him.
t.7.79.18: Having heard those auspicious and sweet words of his, sweet in every syllable, all those women replied in a sweet voice.
t.7.79.19: This fair-hipped lady always remains under our authority; having no husband, she wanders with us through the borders of the forests.
t.7.79.20: Having heard that speech of those women, whose words were indistinct, the twice-born one recited the holy Āvartanī spell.
t.7.79.21: Having learned the whole matter of that king just as it had come to pass, the bull among sages addressed all those women.
t.7.79.23: All of you women will always sustain yourselves on roots, leaves and fruits, and you will obtain husbands known as Kimpuruṣas.
t.7.79.22: Here on the mountain slope, good ones, the Kiṃpuruṣas once dwelt. You too shall dwell on this mountain; let a dwelling place be prepared for you.
t.7.79.24: Having heard the words of the son of Soma, those women, made into Kiṃpuruṣīs, many in number, then dwelt upon the mountain in many places.
